paper_metadata.title: Enhancement of strength-ductility trade-off in a high-entropy alloy through a heterogeneous structure

evidence.quote: Here we present a heterogeneous-structures-architecting strategy, in which we design bulk high-entropy alloys with the largely-enhanced strength-ductility trade-off

evidence.quote: The yield strength of the HEA annealed at 673 K increases to 1,403 ± 20 MPa, and the uniform elongation decreases to 1.2 ± 0.1 %.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical behavior of cold-rolled and annealed Al0.1CoCrFeNi HEAs
evidence.quote: As compared to the HEA annealed at 673 and 1,073 K, the HEA annealed at 873 K displays a good combination of high strength and high ductility. The yield and ultimate strengths are 711 ± 40 and 928 ± 35 MPa, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.3. Mechanical behavior of cold-rolled and annealed Al0.1CoCrFeNi HEAs
evidence.quote: Annealing at 1,073 K causes the HEA to show a high ductility, i.e., the uniform elongation of 42.4 ± 0.6 %, and a low yield strength of 356 ± 13 MPa.
The master alloy was prepared by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity ≥ 99.95 %), and was remelted at least four times ... in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere.

High-density dislocations (HDDs) numbers with dislocation cells (DCs) are observed inside the stretched grains

When annealed at the intermediate temperature of 873 K, the high-entropy alloy possesses a heterogeneous microstructure with three types of grains at multiple length scales, and dislocation-density heterogeneity
High-density dislocations (HDDs) numbers with dislocation cells (DCs) are observed inside the stretched grains
The ATs have a twin thickness of ~ 240 nm, and the stacking faults (SFs) with a thickness of ~ 190 nm are in the recrystallized grains as well (Fig. 2f).
High-density dislocations (HDDs) numbers with dislocation cells (DCs) are observed inside the stretched grains (Fig. 2b), which is estimated as high as ~ 4.56 ± 0.58 × 10^15 m-2
The low-density dislocations (LDDs) with a density of ~ 3.8 ± 1.5 × 10^13 m-2 (the inset of Fig. S6f) also appear at the grain boundary (GB), and inside the partially-recrystallized grains (Fig. 2d).
While in the recrystallized grains, a very low-density dislocation (Fig. 2f) is observed with a density of ~ 1.4 ± 0.65 × 10^12 m-2 (the inset of Fig. S6f).
